Resolves #21603

Drag a desktop app window across the workspace boundary to carry it into a native popup. Bringing the held pointer back returns the same app to the desktop. Releasing outside keeps the popup open, and reloading that document preserves the live window, body, and task. **Pop out window** and **Back to desktop** offer the same transition by click or keyboard.

Evidence: L3 (real Chrome windows and shared App Worker) → physical mouse witness required before merge for D#21204 AC 6. The [v14 cut plan](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7089624234) holds the release for that witness and cross-family review.

## AC Evidence

| Acceptance | Verification |
| --- | --- |
| AC 1 · Held crossing opens and moves a native popup | `WindowTearOut.spec.mjs` observes two real native moves. The same held-drag case on dev `e058be6bb2` reached the drag proxy and failed at popup admission. |
| AC 2 · Re-entry restores the same app and task | The browser case edits Notes, drives one held pointer out and back, then verifies the original App Worker instances and task. A second exit during the same press acquires a fresh popup. |
| AC 3 · Outside release persists, refusal stays reachable | The suite covers outside release, reload of the same popup, subsequent real close, refused admission, and Escape in either window. Unit coverage verifies refused exact close and retry. |
| AC 4 · Record source and platform witness | This PR pins the reviewed commit. [Grace’s design disposition](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7089977239) records what to observe for the physical hold and button path. |

## Deltas from ticket

The v14 production scope includes accessible controls and reload continuity. Both hosts use the shared vessel transaction for native effects and shared embodiment for the live body. An opted-in reload renews the same popup handle for its new document and renderer. The desktop owns workspace geometry and task behavior.

## Test Evidence

- `playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.e2e.mjs --workers=2 test/playwright/e2e/desktop test/playwright/e2e/webdesktop` passed all 31 browser cases at `73de3c3b60`.
- With Chrome's default popup blocking enabled, the production Web Desktop Mail button opened an 880 × 520 native popup. **Back to desktop** closed it, restored the visible Mail window and left one task.
- Emmy provided the independent prototype reload failure and the three existing desktop regression adaptations. [Integration and red reload evidence](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7090042985)

## Cold look

The dark Mail popup uses its first 42 pixels for the return toolbar. The app occupies the full remaining viewport, with the inbox and reading pane visible and no outer scroll. The source retains its normal task entry.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] In the published v14 build, open the Web Desktop and desktop basic example, verify popup-and-return, and verify that a released popup survives reload.

Both reload cases failed on the [original proof](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21603#issuecomment-7089659095), where reload closed the popup and dropped the task. This replay used browser-dispatched pointer input. Tobi’s physical long-hold and native-focus observation remains a separate release step. The production preview is pinned independently of the original experiment.

**A separate cleanup check found an opener-side leak on this head.** In a fresh Chrome context, three successive external closes of detached Mail removed each desktop task. The source window’s `Main.openWindows` registry, however, retained one, then two, then three distinct entries whose `win.closed` was true. All three remained 11 seconds later. On a fourth popup, **Back to desktop** removed its own entry, leaving the earlier three. The actual reload and task-identity results above still hold.

The desktop [external-close acknowledgement](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/73de3c3b60b10257513e71788e798fdc89284dfb/src/desktop/WindowTearOut.mjs#L270) needs to release the exact confirmed-closed opener handle. The [shared observation method](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/73de3c3b60b10257513e71788e798fdc89284dfb/src/Main.mjs#L1303) serves other lifecycle observers and should remain read-only. Replaying the four cycles gives a positive control for a normal return and a negative control for accidental retention. Sophie has the reproducer for this PR.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge** (non-blocking, all four):
  1. Three remote calls can reject unobserved: the unawaited `DragDrop.setConfigs` at `WindowDragZone.mjs:167` and `:242`, and `gesture.retiring.then` at `:171`, which has no catch. A window that goes away mid-gesture would surface an unhandled rejection. A `.catch(() => {})`, as at `WindowTearOut.mjs:278`, closes it.
  2. The e2e refusal arm (`WindowTearOut.spec.mjs:296`) proves the refusal ran (exactly one open attempt) and that the note, the task and the ownership survive. Its single-page check can't fail under the `window.open` stub, though, and it does not assert that the source window gets focus back.
  3. The 10 s reconnect lease for an admitted popup that never connects (`WindowTearOut.mjs:121`, `:287`–`:292`) has no test.
  4. Playwright runs with popup blocking off, so no automated arm meets the real blocker. That is why the physical witness is the gate.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: A browser grants `window.open` only while transient user activation lasts, about 5 s after a press. A held drag can outlive it, so a long hold must fail closed and leave a click path.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: Playwright disables popup blocking, so headless runs cannot witness a refused admission; only a physical hold can.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The tear-out reuses the dock's vessel transaction instead of a second popup lifecycle, so two surfaces share one set of native effects.
